To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a general strategy to construct implicitly defined convex yield functions is presented, and (2) a return-mapping scheme is implemented to integrate the elastic–plastic or –damaging rate equations.

(1) the implicit formulation of the yield function is a general strategy to solve the problems of non-convexity of the yield surface, and (2) a return-mapping algorithm based on the implicit formulation of yield function has been implemented and tested.

(a) a general construction strategy is proposed to define an implicitly convex yield function from a convex yield surface; (b) a return-mapping algorithm is implemented and demonstrated to perform correctly for elastic–plasto–damage rate equations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general and efficient numerical integration scheme to be used in the modelling of the behaviour of granular and rock-like materials.
the development of an implicit return mapping algorithm for the integration of constitutive models for granular and rock-like materials.
the development and validation of an implicit formulation of yield functions for granular and rock-like materials, with the aim of improving their modelling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of the modelling of granular materials, the proposed scheme can be used to integrate any convex yield surface without introducing numerical difficulties.
the scheme presented here is a very general and efficient tool for constitutive integration of rate equations, with the only drawback of introducing a numerical cost.
the scheme is robust and accurate, and should be implemented whenever the yield surface exhibits the aforementioned features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed scheme is general, accurate, efficient and robust.
, for the class of constitutive models considered, the implicit formulation of the yield function is a powerful tool to ensure a robust return-mapping scheme.
we provide a general strategy for the numerical integration of non-convex constitutive equations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed scheme is general, and can be used in any situation where the yield surface is not convex.
, in the context of finite deformation plasticity, a convex yield function may be implicitly defined from any non-convex one, and this allows the use of return-mapping integration algorithms.
, by defining an implicit yield surface, the numerical implementation of a wide class of constitutive models is simplified and made more robust.
